name: Arslanbob Walnut-Fruit Forests
near: Arslanbob (Arstanbap) is ~2–3 km in a straight line from the catalog point; the neighboring village is Gumkhana. The transport hub is Bazar-Korgon on the Bishkek–Osh highway; Jalal-Abad is ~50 km to the south (Trip to Kyrgyzstan).
elev: The village is at about 1,600 m (CBT Arstanbap); other sources give 1,400 m (Journal of Nomads) and 1,700 m (eurasia.travel). The forest covers slopes from roughly 1,500 to 2,000+ m; the waterfall area is at about 2,200 m (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com).
short: One of the largest wild walnut forests in the world, on the slopes of the Fergana and Babash-Ata ranges around the village of Arslanbob, with waterfalls and holy sites.
desc: The Arslanbob walnut-fruit forests are a relict walnut forest mixed with wild apple, pear, cherry plum, cherry, almond and pistachio; the forests hold more than 130 species of trees and shrubs (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The forest around Arslanbob itself is estimated at about 11,000 ha (Journal of Nomads, 2026); the figures of 608,000–700,000 ha found at Trip to Kyrgyzstan and eurasia.travel refer to all the walnut-fruit forests of southern Kyrgyzstan, not to a single valley. Some trees reach 30 m in height and, according to legend, an age of about 1,000 years; the annual nut harvest in the valley is over 1,500 tonnes (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com). Legend links the forest with the campaign of Alexander the Great (329 BC), who supposedly took nuts from here to Greece. The valley has the Big (~80 m) and Small (25–35 m) waterfalls, the holy lake Kel-Mazar and Mount Babash-Ata.
guide: Arslanbob is not a single “forest attraction” but a whole valley: you stay in a guesthouse in the village and walk out into the walnut groves on foot. Start with the Small Waterfall (about 40 minutes on foot) and the panoramic hill above it, and on the second day walk to the Big Waterfall, 80 m high — about 7 km one way. Legend says this is where Alexander the Great took the nuts to Greece — hence the name “Greek” walnut. Come in late September or early October: it is harvest time in the forests, the whole village lives in the woods, and the leaves turn yellow. Bring cash — the ATM in the village is unreliable.
see: Ancient walnut trees around the village; the Small Waterfall (25–35 m, ~1.5 km from the center) with a souvenir market; the Big Waterfall (~80 m, ~7 km); the panoramic hill above the Small Waterfall; the holy lake Kel-Mazar and Mount Babash-Ata (multi-day hikes); natural caves; a walnut oil workshop (CBT tour, 100 som). Sources: Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Journal of Nomads (2026).
skip: You expect “wow” landscapes like Song-Kol — the forest itself is quiet and shady, and the hikes and waterfalls make the bigger impression. You have only one day: the road from Osh/Jalal-Abad takes half a day each way. You would feel uncomfortable in a conservative rural environment (covered clothing is needed).
diff: Easy — walks in the forest and to the Small Waterfall (40 min, 1.5 km); moderate — the Big Waterfall (7 km one way, ~2 h, 4–5 h round trip, the trail is rocky and slippery after rain); hard — a 3-day hike/horse tour to Lake Kel-Mazar with nights in a tent (Journal of Nomads 2026; TripAdvisor; Beyond Wild Places 2026).
when: May to October. For hiking — early May and early October; nut harvest — late September to October, autumn foliage — from late September (Journal of Nomads, Beyond Wild Places 2026). July–August: cooler than Osh, but the guesthouses fill up. In winter (December–January) — backcountry skiing, rental 600 som/day (Journal of Nomads).
hours: The forest is open year-round, 24 hours a day; it is a natural area next to the village with no checkpoint. A fee is charged in summer at the waterfalls (see “Entry cost”); in September, according to 2026 observations, the checkpoint at the Big Waterfall was not operating (Beyond Wild Places).
daytime: Morning is best for the Small Waterfall, before the crowds arrive (Beyond Wild Places, 2026), and for setting off to the Big Waterfall so you can be back by evening. In the daytime the forest is shady and cool.
how: From Osh: a direct marshrutka (minibus) to Arslanbob runs once a day at about 13:30–14:00 from the Osh bus station, 370 som, ~4 h (Beyond Wild Places, 2026). Via Jalal-Abad: Osh – Jalal-Abad (220 som, 2 h) → Bazar-Korgon (60 som, 1 h) → Arslanbob (100 som, ~1.5–2 h). Marshrutkas Bazar-Korgon – Arslanbob run every 30–60 min (eurasia.travel). From Bishkek: shared taxi to Bazar-Korgon (~800–1,200 som), then a marshrutka; 10–12 h in total, ~600 km.
needcar: To get there — yes (marshrutka/taxi to the village). In the village itself and in the forest you go on foot; to the Big Waterfall and the holy sites you can go on horseback through CBT.
self: Yes: the village and the short trails (Small Waterfall, panoramic hill, Big Waterfall along a well-trodden path) can be done without a guide. Deep in the forest the trails are confusing — for longer routes and Kel-Mazar you need a CBT guide (TripAdvisor; Journal of Nomads).
roadtype: To Bazar-Korgon — the paved Bishkek–Osh highway; from Bazar-Korgon to Arslanbob — a paved mountain road through a gorge (eurasia.travel; Beyond Wild Places writes that the transfer is slow). In the forest — dirt trails, rocky and slippery after rain.
traveltime: Osh – Arslanbob: ~4 h on the direct marshrutka, 4–5 h with transfers; Jalal-Abad – Arslanbob: ~2.5 h with a change at Bazar-Korgon; Bishkek – Arslanbob: 10–12 h (Beyond Wild Places 2026; Journal of Nomads; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com).
stay: Guesthouses and CBT homestays in Arslanbob and Gumkhana: about 600 som/person with breakfast, dinner +250 som (Journal of Nomads, updated 2026); private rooms $15–30, more organized ones $20–35 (kgnomad, 2026). Recommended: Guesthouse Ibrahim / CBT Guesthouse 6 (WhatsApp +996 777 733 056, available on Booking.com), Homestay Kelechek; the old Arslanbob tourist base. Through CBT Arstanbap. In July–August and on weekends the best rooms get taken — book in advance.
net: Contradictory: in 2026 Beeline 4G worked well (Beyond Wild Places, 08.2026); in an earlier version of the Journal of Nomads guide, mobile internet was available only on O!. Wi-Fi in guesthouses is unreliable. In the forest and at the Big Waterfall the signal may drop out (unconfirmed).
entry: The forest itself is free. In summer a fee is charged at the waterfalls: Small Waterfall — 10 som, Big Waterfall — about 50 som (Journal of Nomads, updated 04.2026; Beyond Wild Places, 2026 — 50 som, the checkpoint was not operating in September). A tour of the walnut oil workshop — 100 som.
transfer: Marshrutka Osh – Arslanbob 370 som (2026); Osh – Jalal-Abad 220 som, Jalal-Abad – Bazar-Korgon 60 som, Bazar-Korgon – Arslanbob 100 som (Beyond Wild Places, 2026); shared taxi Bishkek – Bazar-Korgon ~800–1,200 som/seat (various years). Private taxi from Jalal-Abad — price not confirmed.
bring: Cash (the ATM is unreliable), covered clothing (conservative village), comfortable trekking shoes (rocky and slippery trails), a rain jacket, water and a snack for the hike to the Big Waterfall; for Kel-Mazar — a tent and sleeping bag (or rent them through CBT).
warn: It is a conservative Muslim community — dress modestly. The ATM in the village is unreliable — bring cash. The trails to the Big Waterfall are rocky and slippery after rain; it is easy to get lost deep in the forest — take a guide for longer routes. The waterfall fees should be small (10–50 som) — check the amount in advance. No border permit is required.
food: Walnuts and walnut oil (tasting at the CBT oil workshop, 100 som with bread), local honey, flatbreads, seasonal fruit and home-cooked dinners at the guesthouse (plov, lagman — typical southern cuisine) (Journal of Nomads; kgnomad).
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.3/5 from 26 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026), No. 1 of 3 attractions in Arslanbob. Pros: shade, quiet, beautiful hikes, waterfalls. Cons: some tourists expected more from the forest itself, complaints about pushy pricing by guides, the trails are easy to lose. Google Maps — rating not collected (the pin is not matched).
p.sum: Arslanbob is a base for 2–3 nights: you get there by marshrutka from Osh (direct one ~13:30–14:00) or via Jalal-Abad and Bazar-Korgon, stay in a CBT-network guesthouse and walk into the forest on foot. Day 1 — the Small Waterfall and Panoramic Hill, day 2 — the Big Waterfall (7 km one way); for the Holy Rock (16 km, 7 h) and the Holy Lake Kel-Mazar (3–4 days) take a guide/horses through CBT Arstanbap. Bring cash in advance: the only reliable ATM is in Bazar-Korgon.

p.iti.0.title: 1 day from Jalal-Abad (bare minimum)
p.iti.0.plan: 07:00 marshrutka Jalal-Abad – Bazar-Korgon, 08:30 change for Arslanbob; 10:30 Small Waterfall and Panoramic Hill; 15:30 lunch; 16:30 return marshrutka. It is tiring — better with an overnight stay.
p.iti.1.title: 2–3 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: arrive from Osh on the direct marshrutka (~18:00), dinner at a CBT house. Day 2: Big Waterfall (7 km, 4–5 h round trip), oil workshop. Day 3: Small Waterfall + Panoramic Hill in the morning, leave on the 06:50 to Osh or on a daytime marshrutka to Bazar-Korgon. With a guide you can replace day 3 with the Holy Rock (7 h).
p.iti.2.title: Combining with other stops on the route
p.iti.2.plan: Osh – Uzgen (minaret) – Arslanbob – Tash-Kumyr – Naryn canyon – Kara-Kul/Toktogul – Ala-Bel – Bishkek; or Arslanbob – Sary-Chelek (via Tash-Kumyr and Aksy, on the way).
p.season: April–May: fresh greenery, hiking, mud is possible. June–August: warm (cooler than Osh), guesthouses are full, the trek to the Holy Lake is open June–September. Late September–October: nut harvest, yellow foliage, the best season. November–March: snow; December–January — backcountry skiing. Fees at the waterfalls (10/50 som) — in summer.
p.budget.economy: ~3,000–4,000 som/person for 2 nights: marshrutka Osh – Arslanbob 370×2 som, guesthouse 600 som×2 + dinners 250×2, waterfall fees 60 som, oil workshop 100 som, snacks ~500 som.
p.budget.comfort: ~$150–300/person: taxi/driver from Osh (~$40–60 one way, estimate), the best guesthouse $25–35, guide $15–25/day, horse $20–40/day; eurasia.travel 3-day tour from $300.
p.permits: Not needed: there is no border zone. In summer there are token fees at the waterfalls (Small 10 som, Big 50 som); in September 2026 the checkpoint at the Big Waterfall was not operating.
p.access: With children — the Small Waterfall (40 min) and walks in the forest; the Big Waterfall — for teenagers with some experience. For older people — the village and short walks. With a stroller — only on the village streets. With a dog — allowed on the trails, but the village is conservative and has many guard dogs.
